Schafkopf Rules

The long Bavarian Schafkopf for four players with 32 German cards: Sauspiel, Wenz and Solo.

The rules

Cards and deal
32 German cards: Acorns, Grass, Hearts and Bells, each Sow (Ace), 10, King, Ober, Unter, 9, 8, 7. Each player gets 8. Points: Sow 11, 10 10, King 4, Ober 3, Unter 2, 9, 8 and 7 nothing - 120 in all. The player after the dealer announces first and leads the first trick.
Announcing
In turn each player passes ("weiter") or announces a game. A later player can take over only with a higher kind of game: Solo beats Wenz, Wenz beats Sauspiel. If all pass, the cards are thrown in.
Sauspiel
Trumps from the highest: the four Obers (Acorn, Grass, Heart, Bell), the four Unters in the same order, then Heart Sow, 10, King, 9, 8, 7. The player calls the Sow of Acorns, Grass or Bells: he must hold a card of that suit himself, but not that Sow. Whoever holds it is his partner - at first only that player knows.
Searching the Sow
When the called suit is led, the holder of the Sow must play it. He may not throw it away before its suit has been led. He may lead its suit only with the Sow itself - unless he holds at least three more cards of that suit; then he may "run away" with another one.
Wenz
Only the four Unters are trumps (Acorn, Grass, Heart, Bell). The Obers stand in their suits between King and 9. The player plays alone against three.
Solo
The player chooses a suit (Acorns, Grass, Hearts or Bells) and plays alone against three. Trumps: the four Obers, the four Unters, then Sow, 10, King, 9, 8, 7 of the chosen suit.
Following suit
You must follow the suit led; Obers and Unters (in the Wenz only the Unters) belong to the trumps, not to their suits. If you cannot follow, you may play any card. The highest trump wins the trick, otherwise the highest card of the suit led.
Winning
The playing side needs 61 points, the others 60. With 91 points the playing side wins Schneider, with 30 or less it loses Schneider. Schwarz: one side takes all eight tricks.
Laufende
The top trumps one side holds without a gap, or misses without a gap, counted from the Acorn Ober (in the Wenz from the Acorn Unter). They count from three, in the Wenz from two.
Tariff
Sauspiel 10 points, Wenz and Solo 50, plus 10 each for Schneider, for Schwarz and for every Laufender. In a Sauspiel each of the two losers pays one winner; in a Wenz or Solo the three others each pay the soloist, or get from him.
The points list
After every game the list shows what each player won or lost; the totals always add up to zero. A thrown-in game is noted without points.

The trumps in the Sauspiel

The four Obers come first, then the four Unters, each in the order Acorn, Grass, Heart, Bell. After them come the Hearts: Sow, 10, King, 9, 8, 7.
